hero.title: Emergency Triage Decision Support
hero.subtitle: Hybrid Manchester Triage classifier combining tree-based ensemble with clinical-note analysis via local language model.

problem.title: The triage problem
problem.subtitle: Why we need decision support
problem.paragraph1: Poland — 8.3M emergency department visits annually. Average assessment wait time: 47 minutes. Triage nurses must classify patients in an average of 90 seconds under severe stress and overload.
problem.paragraph2: Misclassification costs lives. Undertriage (downgrading urgency) has 3× higher clinical cost than overtriage. Project goal: build a system that sees what humans might miss in 90 seconds.

data.title: Training data
data.subtitle: Yale EMMLC — Emergency Medicine ML Challenge
data.description: Anonymized dataset of 558,029 ED visits from Yale-New Haven Hospital. Vitals, demographics, medications, comorbidities, triage notes, 200 chief complaint categories.

features.title: Features
features.engineeredDesc: shock index, MEWS, qSOFA, SIRS, vital × age interactions, time-of-day, missing flags — all computed at runtime.

split.title: Temporal split
split.description: 80/10/10 train/val/test. 10% most recent = test set. No leakage from the future.

layer0.title: Layer 0 — Parser
layer0.description: Raw text → structured JSON. Structured output, temperature 0, physically cannot return invalid JSON.

layer1a.title: Layer 1A — Tabular ML
layer1a.description: CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, RF, ExtraTrees, HistGBT, EBM. Meta-learner: LogReg. SHAP top-5 for every prediction.

layer1b.title: Layer 1B — Clinical NLP
layer1b.description: Analyzes nurse's clinical note. Catches signals that tabular data doesn't contain.

layer2.title: Layer 2 — Synthesis
layer2.description: Combines results from Layer 1A and 1B. Detects conflicts. Generates reasoning for the nurse.

safetyRules.title: Safety rules (hardcoded outside LLM)
safetyRules.rule1: Never go below the minimum of models

models.title: Models
models.subtitle: 7 models, each with a different inductive bias
models.disclaimer: CatBoost = real test set (holdout) results. XGBoost = current CV (tuning in progress). Other models = pre-training estimates.

results.title: Results
results.subtitle: Test set — temporal split, 10% most recent data · 55,802 visits
results.headline: Stacking ensemble wins

step1.title: Nurse input
step1.description: Nurse enters vitals + observation: 'patient 67y, pale, sweaty, chest pain, temp 38.2, HR 118, SBP 95'

step2.title: Parser structures it
step2.description: Llama 3.2 3B converts text to JSON. Structured Output guarantees valid format.

step3.title: ML ensemble
step3.description: 7 models predict the category in parallel. LogReg stacking combines predictions. SHAP explains top 5 features.

step4.title: Clinical NLP
step4.description: MedGemma 27B analyzes the clinical note. Catches 'pale + sweaty + chest pain → ACS risk'.

step5.title: Synthesis and conflicts
step5.description: Qwen3 32B combines results. Detects ML vs NLP conflict. Master rule: escalate, never downgrade.

step6.title: Nurse decides
step6.description: System suggests category + confidence + reasoning. Nurse confirms or rejects. Everything logged (MDR audit).

about.title: About the thesis
about.subtitle: Master's thesis — emergency triage decision support
about.author: Author
about.thesisTitle: Multi-agent decision support system for emergency department triage using machine learning and local language models
about.disclaimer: The system is a proof-of-concept developed as part of a Master's thesis. It has not been deployed clinically and requires validation and certification as a medical device under MDR 2017/745 prior to production use.
